Summary of Changes
------------------

**Major Changes:**
* docs/clustermesh: overhaul Cluster Mesh documentation with a new introduction, improved load-balancing guidance, and Helm-first setup and certificate configuration instructions (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47615, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47351, @MrFreezeex)

**Minor Changes:**
* envoy: demote stale ADS endpoint warning (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47148, @nezdolik)
* Speed up recovery time for disrupted TCP connections that access a DSR-enabled Service. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47881, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47529, @julianwiedmann)

**Bugfixes:**
* azure: Stop issuing redundant CiliumNode status updates on every IPAM sync when the node's Azure interfaces are unchanged. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47449, @jaredledvina)
* bpf: dsr: don't look for TCP header on fragmented packets (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47881, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47640, @julianwiedmann)
* bpf: hostfw: tolerate unknown CT protocols and rely on policies (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47621, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47343, @smagnani96)
* clustermesh: fix MCS-API CRD install/upgrade when clustermesh-apiserver is started before the CRD version is actually installed (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47824, @MrFreezeex)
* datapath: turn ARP off on the base devices before bringing them up (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47838, @aanm)
* endpoint/watchdog: Avoid warning about endpoints being deleted (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47625, @christarazi)
* endpoint: Fix silent CIDR policy bypass and traffic drops after agent restart (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47954, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47880, @weizhoublue)
* envoy.httpUpstreamLingerTimeout accepts `0` as a chart value and templates into configmap. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47741, @jdw6359)
* envoy: restore http-idle-timeout as the route idle timeout source (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47583, @aanm)
* Fix a BPF verifier reject on pre-v5.12 kernels, when IPv6 is enabled. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47765, @julianwiedmann)
* Fix a deadlock in the shutdown of Cilium operator related to CiliumEndpointSlices. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47967, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47802, @bimmlerd)
* Fix a NetworkPolicy update being ignored for up to two minutes when it arrived while an endpoint was waiting for its security identity to be resolved after a pod relabel. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47727, @aanm)
* Fix a spurious "unable to find ifindex for interface MAC" agent warning on EKS ENI IPAM by waiting for the ENI netlink interface before configuring ingress routes and rules. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47295, @aanm)
* Fix abnormal ip allocation caused by hostnetwork pod (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47552, @haozhangami)
* Fix unintended RevDNAT for client-to-pod TCP connections, when an identical connection was previously established through a DSR Service. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47881, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47593, @julianwiedmann)
* fix: allow setting endpointPolicyUpdateTimeoutDuration in helm (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47754, @weizhoublue)
* Fixed an issue where an HTTPRoute referencing a Gateway with mixed listener protocols (e.g. HTTP and TCP) was incorrectly rejected with `NotAllowedByListeners` when the TCP listener had an explicit `AllowedRoutes.Kinds` restriction. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#46842, @pidreher)
* gateway-api/gamma: refresh CEC owner refs on route recreation (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47954, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47840, @mhofstetter)
* gateway-api: mark unresolved backend service ports in route status (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47766, @mhofstetter)
* gateway-api: preserve duplicate HTTPRoute rule precedence (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#46696, @thorn3r)
* gateway-api: prevent conflicted listeners from reaching ingestion (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47457, @asauber)
* gateway-api: requeue L4/TLS routes on ServiceImport updates (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47702, @mhofstetter)
* gateway-api: sync ListenerSet TLS secrets on ListenerSet events (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47627, @mhofstetter)
* ipcache: fix CIDR reference counter to use canonical prefixes (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47208, @iwanhae)
* l2announcer: re-evaluate services on frontend changes (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47579, @mhofstetter)
* Log the correct route kind when the Gateway API operator fails to list TLSRoutes for a backend Service (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47954, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47826, @mehrdadbn9)
* operator: Emit startup logs in the configured log format (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47954, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47890, @HadrienPatte)
* Resolve a endpoint manager crash for restored endpoints with verbose policy logging enabled. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47844, @bimmlerd)
* standalone-dns-proxy: return an error when no endpoint is found (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47954, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47791, @vipul-21)
* wireguard: Unsubscribe node handler on shutdown (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47614, @HadrienPatte)

**CI Changes:**
* .github: add python3-scapy for BPF unit tests (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47535, @msune)
* .github: run all quarantined EKS tests in a single tolerated step (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47534, @aanm)
* .github: Run envoy image check against PR content (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47792, @joestringer)
* .github: Simplify permissions for image linter workflow (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47753, @joestringer)
* .github: suppress spurious encryption leak reports for node-to-pod DNS requests going through proxy (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47470, @atykhyy)
* .github: test the default ENI behaviour on the EKS pull request leg (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47569, @aanm)
* ariane: move kind-proxy-embedded and kubespray workflows to /test (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47743, @giorio94)
* bpf/complexity-tests: Cover L7 LB (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47060, @pchaigno)
* ci: build race images on push events so conformance-race works on stable branches (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47609, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47608, @aanm)
* ci: build race images on push in the stable image builders (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47609, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47616, @aanm)
* ci: draft renovate PRs until ciliumbot auto-approval (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47364, @mhofstetter)
* ci: fix filtering out md files in bpf checks (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47605, @nebril)
* ci: migrate set-commit-status to cilium/actions (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47771, @bogdankrasko)
* ci: skip etcd log fetch when kvstore was never started (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47801, @aanm)
* Fix missing `events_map_rate_limit` complexity coverage (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47691, @pchaigno)
* gha/kubespray: run on schedule, rather than on every push (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47731, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47719, @giorio94)
* gha/lvh-kind: respect Kind image version also when config is provided (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47731, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47703, @giorio94)
* gha: don't install LLVM and Clang in integration tests workflow (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47731, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47717, @giorio94)
* gha: fix checkout of trusted branch in smoke and k8s-kind workflows (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47731, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47724, @giorio94)
* images/scripts: Validate Envoy image vars against sed injection (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47205, @MasloMaslane)
* Revert "gha: don't install LLVM and Clang in integration tests workflow" (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47780, @giorio94)
* test(bpf): parallelize eBPF test compilation (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47954, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47426, @lconnery)
* test/cyclonus: log the JUnit XML instead of copying it from a dead pod (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47725, @aanm)
* test: allowlist the leader election read timeout in ginkgo log check (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47612, @aanm)

**Misc Changes:**
* Added documentation for running Cilium in CNI chaining mode on Oracle Kubernetes Engine (OKE) with VCN-Native Pod Networking. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#46116, @amaanx86)
* allocator: fix flake in TestWatchRemoteKVStore (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47455, @giorio94)
* bpf/nat: Move IPv6 nat entry to map (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47762, @pchaigno)
* bpf: conntrack: Reduce stack usage of `ct_create{4,6}` (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47582, @dylandreimerink)
* bpf: dsr: only require DSR-info on SYN packet (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47881, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47592, @julianwiedmann)
* bpf: dsr: re-use TCP SYN flag from CT lookup in remote-backend path (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47881, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47388, @julianwiedmann)
* bpf: lb: use dedicated new_backend bool (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47881, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47841, @julianwiedmann)

signals.title: bpf: migrate non-branching config macros to runtime configuration
signals.text: The current step in the clang-freedom (pre-compiled eBPF programs) journey is to start transitioning compile time configuration to load-time (runtime) configuration. The necessary agent and loader infrastructure has been merged. Runtime configuration can be defined with [`DECLARE_CONFIG` and `NODE_CONFIG`](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/bpf/lib/static_data.h). See [Configuring the Datapath](https://docs.cilium.io/en/latest/contributing/development/datapath_config) in the Cilium Developer docs for guidelines and principles. ~~This issue specifically tracks variables which do not influence control flow by enabling or disabling certain code paths. Variables used in `#ifdef`/`#if` and `if(is_defined(...))` will be converted in 1.19 since dead code elimination only really landed in Linux 5.5, and Cilium 1.18 targets Linux 5.4 which will go EOL at the end of 2025.~~ 1.19 targets Linux 5.10. We can migrate branching macros, too. Additionally, https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/41628 shipped in 1.19 which added dead code detection in the agent to avoid loading unused maps and tail calls. Branching macros can now safely be ported. This issue is for migrating `node_config.h` and `WriteNodeConfig` entries to `config.Node`, as well as some leftover per-object configs in `ep_config.h`. Through this issue, we can coordinate work and keep an overview. If you want to work on a particular (set of) variable(s), drop a comment and we'll spin out an issue or assign you to a list item. The list may change over time and may grow as we find more work in this category. When migrating variables, do a quick search through [Paul's macro documentation](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/15379#issuecomment-897441189) for a good docstring to use in `DECLARE_CONFIG`. - [ep_config.h](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/bpf/ep_config.h) - [x] HOST_EP_ID - [x] DIRECT_ROUTING_DEV_IFINDEX - [node_config.h](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/bpf/node_config.h) - [x] CLUSTER_ID - [x] CILIUM_*_IFINDEX, CILIUM_*_MAC (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43474) - [x] TUNNEL_PORT, TUNNEL_PROTOCOL (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43520) - [x] KERNEL_HZ, ENABLE_JIFFIES (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43112) - [x] L2_ANNOUNCEMENTS(_MAX_LIVENESS) (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/42587) - [x] EPHEMERAL_MIN (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43564) - [x] IS_L3_DEV, NATIVE_DEV_MAC_BY_IFINDEX (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/39116 & https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43680) - [x] CLUSTER_ID_MAX (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/42478) - [x] IDENTITY_{LEN,MAX} (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43507) - [x] VTEP_MASK (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43112) - [x] NODEPORT_PORT_* (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43680) - [x] IPV4_LOOPBACK (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/38818) - [x] NAT_46X64_PREFIX (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43799) - [x] CIDR_IDENTITY_RANGE_{START,END} (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44223) - [x] HASH_INIT{4,6}_SEED (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44190) - [x] EVENTS_MAP_* (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44795) - [ ] VLAN_FILTER (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/38721) - [x] Reserved security IDs (HOST_ID, WORLD_ID, ect.) (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45009) - [ ] CT_* (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/47537) - [ ] IPV4_{MASK,GATEWAY,LOOPBACK} (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/38818) - [ ] IPV4_SNAT_* (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/48065) - [x] IPV4_INTER_CLUSTER_SNAT (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/47680) - [ ] IPV6_SNAT_* - [ ] SNAT_COLLISION_RETRIES - [x] MONITOR_AGGREGATION (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/47366) - [x] MTU (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/46219) - [x] DIRECT_ROUTING_DEV_IFINDEX - [ ] IPV{4,6}_DIRECT_ROUTING (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/47888) - [x] IPV{4,6}_RSS_PREFIX[_BITS] (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/47363) - [x] LB_SELECTION (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/46729) - [x] WG_IFINDEX, WG_PORT (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/41137) - [x] STRICT_IPV4_NET[_SIZE] (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/47358) - [ ] IPV4_ENCRYPT_IFACE - [ ] HOST_NETNS_COOKIE - [ ] ENCAP4_IFINDEX, ENCAP6_IFINDEX - [ ] LRU_MEM_FLAVOR - [ ] PREALLOCATE_MAPS, NO_COMMON_MEM_MAPS - [x] ENABLE_MKE, MKE_HOST (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/47979) - [ ] DSR_ENCAP_MODE

signals.title: MTU issue for large UDP packets with native routing and DSR
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues: this is very similar to #32601 ### Version equal or higher than v1.17.4 and lower than v1.18.0 ### What happened? The situation is almost the same as the one in the other issue: I have an environment with native routing and DSR, with a UDP (SIP) service with 3 endpoints running on 3 different nodes. There are some large (>2000) UDP packets being sent from outside the cluster to one of the endpoint, which get correctly fragmented following the ICMP instructions sent by path MTU discovery. Luckily pmtu accounts for the 8 bytes header added for DSR, but it does not for any other possible header (like VLAN tags). This causes the packet to possibly be higher than the default network MTU and being dropped. I am not really sure which entity is dropping the packets, as I don't see them reaching Cilium. I've read somewhere that some routers drop packets with unknown options headers when they receive too many of them, so that might be a problem. I also tried to set Cilium's MTU to 1450, but the problem perists. Things seems to work when client and k8s cluster are on the same network, but if they are on two different VLANs (which can of course reach each other) then the packet is that bit larger that gets dropped, or at least this is my assumption ### How can we reproduce the issue? 1. Install Cilium with the following values on a multi-node k3s cluster ```yaml k8sServiceHost: k8s.kubelab.alea.lab k8sServicePort: 6443 kubeProxyReplacement: true ipv4NativeRoutingCIDR: "10.42.0.0/16" ipam: mode: kubernetes operator: clusterPoolIPv4PodCIDRList: "10.42.0.0/16" bpf: masquerade: false nodePort: enabled: true externalIPs: enabled: true l7Proxy: false hubble: relay: enabled: true ui: enabled: true l2announcements: enabled: true leaseDuration: 3s leaseRenewDeadline: 1.5s leaseRetryPeriod: 1s k8sClientRateLimit: qps: 170 burst: 200 healthChecking: true endpointHealthChecking: enabled: true tunnelProtocol: "" routingMode: native loadBalancer: mode: dsr dsrDispatch: opt socketLB: enabled: true hostNamespaceOnly: true autoDirectNodeRoutes: true MTU: 0 pmtuDiscovery: enabled: true ``` 2. Create a Cilium L2 announcement policy and LoadBalancer IP Pool 3. Deploy a UDP server with 3 replicas, and expose it with a LoadBalancer service 4. Send a UDP packet to the Loadbalancer IP with a size higher than 1500 ### Cilium Version cilium-cli: v0.18.3 compiled with go1.24.2 on linux/amd64 cilium image (default): v1.17.2 cilium image (stable): v1.17.3 cilium image (running): 1.17.3 ### Kernel Version Linux kubelab-w07 5.15.0-307.178.5.el8uek.x86_64 #2 SMP Wed Mar 19 13:00:52 PDT 2025 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux ### Kubernetes Version Client Version: v1.31.3 Kustomize Version: v5.4.2 Server Version: v1.32.3+k3s1 ### Regression _No response_ ### Sysdump _file is too large_ ### Relevant log output ```shell ``` ### Anything else? _No response_ ### Cilium Users Document - [ ] Are you a user of Cilium? Please add yourself to the [Users doc](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/USERS.md) ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

signals.title: WireGuard node-to-node encryption: oversized packets cause fragmentation, and BPF fragment tracking drops most second fragments
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.19.3 and lower than v1.20.0 ### What happened? We identified two seemingly related issues when using Cilium's WireGuard-based node-to-node encryption with host-network pods on nodes. 1. WireGuard encapsulation produces packets exceeding the physical NIC MTU, causing IP fragmentation that should not occur. This is related to https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/23917 and _might_ be addressed by https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45940. However when artificially setting the cilium_wg0 interface MTU to a lower value, the issue does not disappear completely, suggesting traffic originating on the node's interface (host-network pods) might not really benefit from it. I plan to revisit this after I'm able to test the above official fix. 2. Most second fragments are dropped by Cilium's BPF TC ingress program with DROP_FRAG_NOT_FOUND ("First logical datagram fragment not found"). edit: after digging a bit more, I wouldn't be surprised if this was just caused by a simple out-of-order reassembly, which doesn't seem supported yet https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/25709#issuecomment-1969602232 As a hacky workaround, setting the WG interface MTU to 9000-95, PLUS clamping TCP connections on the physical NIC to 9000-95-40 prevents fragmented packets and seems it resolve both issues (only for TCP). ### How can we reproduce the issue? Cloud provider: OCI (Oracle Cloud Infrastructure) Datapath mode: VXLAN tunnel + WireGuard encryption with Node encryption enabled Physical NIC MTU: 9000 Host-network pods: yes (both sides of the connection) Establish a normal TCP connection between the 2 pods, sending relevant amount of data. Asking some help to an LLM, this is the analysis. Attaching in case it can provide some orientation, but it's not something I could easily verify/dispute. Would appreciate some guidance on how to further narrow this down, or insight from maintainers on known limitations of the fragment tracking under concurrent multi-queue processing. > All drops are second fragments: Length=84 (20 IP header + 64 payload), FragOffset=1122 (× 8 = 8976 bytes offset), Flags= empty (last fragment, no MF bit). > pwru trace on the receiving node, filtered for second fragments (ip[6:2] & 0x1fff = 1122), shows two divergent paths at tcf_classify: > Path A — DROP (majority of packets): dev_gro_receive → inet_gro_receive → packet_rcv → tcf_classify → skb_ensure_writable → kfree_skb_reason(SKB_DROP_REASON_TC_INGRESS) ← BPF returns DROP The packet never reaches ip_rcv_core. The BPF program dropped it because the map lookup returned NULL. > Path B — SUCCESS (minority of packets): dev_gro_receive → inet_gro_receive → packet_rcv → tcf_classify → skb_ensure_writable → ip_rcv_core → nf_hook_slow → ip_defrag ← BPF returned OK → ip_frag_queue → inet_frag_queue_insert → inet_frag_reasm_prepare → skb_clone → skb_morph → [cilium_wg0 thread]: __skb_to_sgvec → consume_skb ← WireGuard decrypts The BPF program found the map entry, returned OK, and kernel ip_defrag successfully reassembled and delivered the packet to WireGuard. > What we cannot determine We can observe that the cilium_ipv4_frag_datagrams map lookup succeeds for some second fragments and fails for others, but we cannot determine why from outside the BPF program. The map is BPF_MAP_TYPE_LRU_HASH (global, not per-CPU), so it should be visible across all CPUs. > Possible causes we considered but could not verify: A timing/ordering issue where the second fragment's BPF execution races against the first fragment's map write (e.g., because the NIC's RSS dispatches them to different RX queues, and both BPF programs run concurrently on different CPUs) An issue with the first fragment's path — perhaps it is redirected or consumed before map_update_elem executes in some code paths An LRU eviction issue under high traffic The first fragment path is not visible in our pwru trace (we only filtered for second fragments). ### Cilium Users Document - [ ] Are you a user of Cilium? signals.title: Gateway API L7LB north-south traffic still dropped on 1.19.4 when LB VIP is announced on a VLAN subinterface (not a bridge)
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue? - Related: #43819, #44187 (same north-south L7LB class). This adds a data point: the merged fixes #44658 / #45582 do **not** resolve it when the ingress device is a **VLAN subinterface** rather than a Linux bridge. ### What happened? External (north-south) TCP to a Gateway API L7 LoadBalancer VIP (an endpoint-less `type: LoadBalancer` Service flagged `[LoadBalancer, l7-load-balancer]`) is silently dropped before reaching Envoy, on **Cilium 1.19.4** — which contains both #44658 and #45582. The LB VIP is advertised via Cilium L2 announcements on a **VLAN subinterface** (`vsw0.4042@uplink0`, a Hetzner vSwitch VLAN), not a Linux bridge. `br_netfilter` is loaded and `net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables=1`. Observed on a request to the VIP from an external client and from a pod: - `cilium monitor -v` shows the redirect decision firing: `-> proxy port 19052 ... <client> -> <vip>:4318 tcp SYN` (this is new in 1.19.4; on 1.18.10 there was **no** datapath event at all — so #44658/#45582 did change behavior). - But the packet **never reaches the Envoy socket**: `tcpdump -i lo port 19052` shows zero traffic; no SYN-ACK egresses on any interface; the client times out. - `cilium monitor --type drop` shows nothing (drop is not in the BPF datapath). - Routing primitives are all correct: `ip rule` has `from all fwmark 0x200/0xf00 lookup 2004`, table `2004` has `local default dev lo`, Envoy is listening on `127.0.0.1:19052` (`SO_REUSEPORT`), `rp_filter=0`. - **Host-netns-originated** traffic to the same VIP works (socket-LB path). - Ruled out: host firewall (tested with it disabled), and `net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables=0` (tested — no change). This looks like the `MARK_MAGIC_TO_PROXY` + punt-to-stack / TPROXY-in-PREROUTING path from #36383, where the second PREROUTING pass is skipped (so the TPROXY rule never delivers to the socket). #44658 adds a hairpin fallback **gated on the device being a bridge**; our ingress device is a VLAN subinterface, so that fallback appears not to engage, and #45582’s `ctx->mark` fix doesn’t help here either. ### Question for maintainers Should the #44658 hairpin / #45582 fix also cover **non-bridge** netdevs (e.g. VLAN subinterfaces) when `br_netfilter` + `bridge-nf-call-iptables=1` cause `ip_sabotage_in()` to skip the second PREROUTING pass? Is there a recommended config to force the hairpin path for L7LB on such devices? ### Cilium Version 1.19.4 (upgraded from 1.18.10; behavior changed but issue persists) ### Kernel Version 6.8.0-117-generic (Ubuntu 24.04) ### Kubernetes Version v1.34 (k3s) ### Relevant config - `kubeProxyReplacement: true`, `l7Proxy: true`, `loadBalancer.l7.backend: envoy` - `l2announcements.enabled: true`; LB-IPAM VIP announced on a VLAN subinterface - Gateway API (native Cilium GatewayClass), TLS-terminating listeners on 443/4317/4318

signals.title: Public IP SNAT Configurability
signals.text: ### Is your proposed feature related to a problem? If you add a public/external IP address to a network interface, Cilium performs SNAT on egress traffic. If you add multiple public IP addresses, Cilium only performs SNAT on the first one. Also, it sends all egress traffic with that SNAT address. Previous discussion/research [here](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/discussions/46167) ### Describe the feature you'd like I want to be able to control what is SNATed, and what is not. Think of having a default cluster/LAN egress. This goes out via the default ISP. Then, I have a service that should be SNATed on public IP 1. Repeat with multiple public IP addresses. Currently, the workaround I need to do is to only use LAN IP addresses, and perform SNAT at the router level. I would much rather be able to specify how to shape the traffic at the Cilium level and have the router just move traffic based on pure routing rules. ### Notify relevant community channels _No response_ ### (Optional) Describe your proposed solution _No response_

signals.title: Pre-flight ahead of 1.20 upgrade doesn't drop CiliumNodeConfig v2alpha1 CRD
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.20.0 and lower than v1.21.0 ### What happened? [Asked first on Slack](https://cilium.slack.com/archives/C1MATJ5U5/p1785758062847279), but another person confirmed experiencing this too. One of the upgrade notes mentioned the upgrade of `CiliumNodeConfig` from `v2alpha1` to `v2`. I checked beforehand: ```sh $ kubectl get ciliumnodeconfigs.v2alpha1.cilium.io --all-namespaces Warning: cilium.io/v2alpha1 CiliumNodeConfig will be deprecated in cilium v1.16; use cilium.io/v2 CiliumNodeConfig No resources found ``` I then installed the preflight check: ```sh $ helm install cilium-preflight oci://quay.io/cilium/charts/cilium --version 1.20.0 \ --namespace kube-system \ --set preflight.enabled=true \ --set agent=false \ --set operator.enabled=false Pulled: quay.io/cilium/charts/cilium:1.20.0 Digest: sha256:8009baed89d99fd84f7ee5cfdbf3a1fae8153452132549833956b6aca8b9d738 NAME: cilium-preflight LAST DEPLOYED: Mon Aug 3 13:32:10 2026 NAMESPACE: kube-system STATUS: deployed REVISION: 1 DESCRIPTION: Install complete TEST SUITE: None NOTES: You have successfully ran the preflight check. Now make sure to check the number of READY pods is the same as the number of running cilium pods. Then make sure the cilium preflight deployment is also marked READY 1/1. If you have an issues please refer to the CNP Validation section in the upgrade guide. Your release version is 1.20.0. For any further help, visit https://docs.cilium.io/en/v1.20/gettinghelp ``` Now, I merged my upgrade PR so Flux rolled out the upgrade from 1.19.6 to 1.20.0. However, the operator pods end up in `CrashLoopBackOff` with this error around `CiliumNodeConfig`: ``` time=2026-08-03T11:52:00.976886093Z level=error msg="Start hook failed" module=operator function="apis.createCRDs.func1 (.../k8s/apis/cell.go:64)" error="unable to create CRDs: Unable to create custom resource definition: CustomResourceDefinition.apiextensions.k8s.io \"ciliumnodeconfigs.cilium.io\" is invalid: status.storedVersions[0]: Invalid value: \"v2alpha1\": missing from spec.versions; v2alpha1 was previously a storage version, and must remain in spec.versions until a storage migration ensures no data remains persisted in v2alpha1 and removes v2alpha1 from status.storedVersions" ``` Now the CNP validator didn't return anything: ``` $ kubectl logs -n kube-system deployment/cilium-pre-flight-check -c cnp-validator --previous Error from server (BadRequest): previous terminated container "cnp-validator" in pod "cilium-pre-flight-check-f65fdb894-qthmk" not found ``` The `v2alpha1` storage version CRD hasn't been dropped during the upgrade. ### How can we reproduce the issue? I ran an upgrade of Cilium v1.19.6 to v1.20.0 on my homelab cluster. I'm not sure if this is reproducible for everyone though. ### Cilium Version Upgrade from Cilium v1.19.6 to v1.20.0. ### Kernel Version 6.18.39-talos arm64 on Raspberri Pi CM4 ### Kubernetes Version v1.36.3 ### Regression _No response_ ### Sysdump [cilium-sysdump-20260805-163930.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30748735/cilium-sysdump-20260805-163930.zip) ### Relevant log output ```shell ``` ### Anything else? _No response_ ### Cilium Users Document - [ ] Are you a user of Cilium? Please add yourself to the [Users doc](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/USERS.md) ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

signals.title: Option to disable Prometheus annotations in Helm Chart
signals.text: ### Is your proposed feature related to a problem? Datadog has a Cilium integration that makes Cilium metrics free. This is great, as custom metrics are expensive and Cilium has a lot of metrics. However, the Prometheus metrics port needs to be present for the integration to work but in the Helm Chart it is not possible to enable the port without also enabling the Prometheus scraping annotations. This means that the datadog agent picks up the scraping annotations and sends all of the metrics to Datadog as custom metrics in addition to the metrics coming from the integration. ### Describe the feature you'd like I would like an option in the helm chart to disable Prometheus Scraping Annotations but not disable the metrics port. ### Notify relevant community channels _No response_ ### (Optional) Describe your proposed solution _No response_

signals.title: ipcache: max_entries is hard-coded at 512k with no configuration path, blocks clusters beyond ~500k routable IPs
signals.text: ### Is your proposed feature related to a problem? **Description** cilium_ipcache_v2 is created with a hard-coded capacity of 512,000 entries (MaxEntries in pkg/maps/ipcache/ipcache.go, propagated to the datapath as IPCACHE_MAP_SIZE). Unlike most other large BPF maps, there is no CLI flag to override it, and --bpf-map-dynamic-size-ratio does not cover it. Since the ipcache holds one entry per routable IP (pods, nodes, CIDR/FQDN identities), this constant is a hard ceiling on cluster size: at ~10k nodes with a realistic pod density, the map saturates. When the map is full, upserts fail with ENOSPC and the entry is dropped (a warn log is the only signal). Traffic to/from the affected IPs is then misclassified, which at minimum breaks policy enforcement for those endpoints. We are targeting cluster size that already hit this limit in scale testing. **What we observed (scale test)** Scale test on a setup, 10k virtual nodes, ~700k pods target, Cilium : Agent logs — upserts silently lost: ``` time=2026-07-20T21:57:41Z level=warn msg="unable to update bpf map" module=agent.datapath.ipcache-bpf-listener ipAddr="{IP:10.6.155.145 Mask:ffffffff}" identity="{Source:custom-resource ID:43285 ...}" modification=Upsert error="update map cilium_ipcache_v2: update: no space left on device" ``` Map confirmed full on the node: ``` # bpftool map show id 331 331: lpm_trie name cilium_ipcache_ flags 0x81 key 24B value 24B max_entries 512000 memlock 43008000B # bpftool map dump id 331 | grep -c "key:" 512000 ``` Note the memory numbers: the full map accounts for 43 MB of kernel memory (84 B/entry), on a node with 3.7 GiB available. Memory is not the constraint; max_entries alone is. Environment: Cilium v1.18.5, kernel > 6.8.x, 10k virtual nodes, ~700k pods target. **Precedent exists, including for LPM tries.** Three LPM-trie map families are already size-configurable through the exact mechanism we are proposing: the egress gateway policy maps (--egress-gateway-policy-map-max -> EGRESS_POLICY_MAP_SIZE), the per-endpoint policy map, an LPM trie since the wildcard-ports rework (--bpf-policy-map-max -> POLICY_MAP_SIZE, wired in pkg/maps/policymap/cell.go), and the LB source-range maps (--bpf-lb-source-range-map-max -> LB4/LB6_SRC_RANGE_MAP_SIZE, falling back to --bpf-lb-map-max). Same flag pattern for hash maps: --bpf-node-map-max, --bpf-auth-map-max, etc. ### Describe the feature you'd like We'd like the ipcache map size to be configurable, e.g. via a --bpf-ipcache-map-max agent flag defaulting to the current 512,000, following the exact pattern already used for the egress gateway policy map, the per-endpoint policy map, and the LB source-range maps (all LPM tries, see precedent in the previous section). Raising it is what stands between us and 10,000-node clusters. We've done our best to reason from the code and git history, but that only goes so far, there may be context (past incidents, discussions, design intent) that isn't visible from us or we may have missed. That's really what we're hoping to learn here: - Is there a structural reason (verifier, datapath, operational) for the 512k ceiling that we're missing? ### Notify relevant community channels _No response_ ### (Optional) Describe your proposed solution _No response_

signals.title: Hubble Relay does not terminate, gRPC health server remains running
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.20.0 and lower than v1.21.0 ### What happened? Hubble Relay does not fully terminate after receiving SIGTERM. The Relay server shuts down and the log reports Server stopped, but the Relay process remains running until the Kubernetes termination grace period expires and the pod is killed with SIGTERM. The dedicated gRPC health server on port 4222 remains listening after the main Relay server has already stopped. ## Cause `Server.Serve()` starts both the gRPC and the separate gRPC health Server and waits for all of them to return. The current Server.Stop() stops the main server with: `s.server.Stop()` but does not stop: `s.grpcHealthServer` This appears to leave the health server listening on port 4222, preventing `errgroup.Wait()` in `Server.Serve()` from returning. The health server appears to have been introduced in: [b1f246567b72 ("hubble/relay: Update health server to check connectivity")](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/commit/b1f246567b7233fdd9a3edcbbe102415d3911fe4) ### How can we reproduce the issue? Run Hubble Relay in Kubernetes. Start termination of the Relay pod, for example as part of a node drain. Observe the Relay logs: ``` Stopping server... Server stopped ``` The pod remains in Terminating and the container remains in a running state. Inspect the Relay process network namespace after Server stopped: `sudo nsenter -t "$PID" -n ss -ltnp` Port 4222 is still in LISTEN state while the main Relay listener is gone. A SIGQUIT stack dump taken showed Server.Serve() waiting in: ``` sync.(*WaitGroup).Wait golang.org/x/sync/errgroup.(*Group).Wait github.com/cilium/cilium/pkg/hubble/relay/server.(*Server).Serve ``` ### Cilium Version 1.20.0 ### Kernel Version 5.14.0 ### Kubernetes Version 1.36.3 ### Regression _No response_ ### Sysdump _No response_ ### Relevant log output ```shell sync.(*WaitGroup).Wait golang.org/x/sync/errgroup.(*Group).Wait github.com/cilium/cilium/pkg/hubble/relay/server.(*Server).Serve ``` ### Anything else? _No response_ ### Cilium Users Document - [ ] Are you a user of Cilium? Please add yourself to the [Users doc](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/USERS.md) ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

signals.title: Gateway API: 503 connection timeout for same-node backends with L2 announcements and VXLAN tunnel mode
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.20.0 and lower than v1.21.0 ### What happened? Gateway API with L2 announcements and VXLAN tunnel mode produces 503 "upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers. reset reason: connection timeout" for **all backend pods running on the same node that holds the L2 VIP lease**. Backend pods on other nodes work perfectly. The pattern is deterministic and follows the L2 lease holder: - When `node-a` holds the lease: all backends on `node-a` return 503, all backends on other nodes return 200 - When the lease moves (e.g. after a cilium restart): the failures follow the lease to the new holder node Envoy admin cluster stats confirm the pattern. Cross-node connectivity from regular pods (both with and without hostNetwork) works fine - this is specific to the envoy TPROXY path. `proxy-use-original-source-address` is hardcoded to `true` by the Helm chart when `kubeProxyReplacement: true`, and cannot be overridden via Helm values. This might be the root cause: envoy connects to same-node pods using the external client's source IP via TPROXY, and the response packet from the backend pod cannot route back to envoy correctly in VXLAN tunnel mode. **Please note that I did this research with Claude. I haven't tested the workaround yet.** ### How can we reproduce the issue? **Environment:** 3-node k3s cluster on Raspberry Pi (arm64), Ubuntu 26.04, kernel 7.0.0-1016-raspi **Cluster topology:** - `jarvis` (control-plane): 192.168.10.100, pod CIDR 10.0.1.0/24 - `node-a` (worker): 192.168.10.101, pod CIDR 10.0.2.0/24 - `node-b` (worker): 192.168.10.102, pod CIDR 10.0.0.0/24 **Steps:** 1. Install Cilium with the following Helm values: ```yaml kubeProxyReplacement: true gatewayAPI: enabled: true l2announcements: enabled: true l7Proxy: true bpf: tproxy: true devices: eth0 envoy: enabled: true securityContext: capabilities: envoy: - NET_ADMIN - SYS_ADMIN - NET_BIND_SERVICE keepCapNetBindService: true socketLB: enabled: true hostNamespaceOnly: false operator: replicas: 1 ``` 2. Create a CiliumLoadBalancerIPPool and CiliumL2AnnouncementPolicy: ```yaml apiVersion: cilium.io/v2alpha1 kind: CiliumLoadBalancerIPPool metadata: name: gateway-lan-pool spec: blocks: - start: 192.168.10.50 stop: 192.168.10.50 --- apiVersion: cilium.io/v2alpha1 kind: CiliumL2AnnouncementPolicy metadata: name: l2-announcement spec: interfaces: - ^eth0 loadBalancerIPs: true ``` 3. Create a Gateway with multiple HTTPS listeners and HTTPRoutes pointing to services on different nodes 4. Observe that backends on the node holding the L2 lease (check via `kubectl get leases -n kube-system | grep cilium-l2announce`) return 503, while backends on other nodes work **Verification commands:** ```bash # Check which node holds the lease kubectl get leases -n kube-system cilium-l2announce-default-cilium-gateway-http-gateway -o jsonpath='{.spec.holderIdentity}' # Check envoy cluster stats (run on the cilium pod of the lease-holding node) kubectl exec -n kube-system <cilium-pod> -- cilium-dbg envoy admin clusters | grep -E "(cx_connect_fail|rq_success|rq_error)" # Test cross-node connectivity from a regular pod (works fine) kubectl run tmp --rm -i --restart=Never --image=curlimages/curl -- curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://<backend-pod-ip>:<port> # Test from hostNetwork pod on the lease-holding node (also works fine) kubectl run tmp --rm -i --restart=Never --overrides='{"spec":{"hostNetwork":true,"nodeName":"<lease-holder>"}}' --image=curlimages/curl -- curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://<backend-pod-ip>:<port> ``` Both connectivity tests return 200, proving the issue is specific to the envoy TPROXY path, not general network connectivity. ### Relevant log output Curl response from the gateway for a same-node backend: ``` > GET / HTTP/1.1 > Host: argocd.jarvis-home.dev < HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable < content-length: 91 < content-type: text/plain < server: envoy upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers. reset reason: connection timeout ``` Envoy admin cluster stats for the failing backend (same node as lease holder): ``` argocd:argocd-server:80::10.0.2.4:8080::cx_active::0 argocd:argocd-server:80::10.0.2.4:8080::cx_connect_fail::14 argocd:argocd-server:80::10.0.2.4:8080::cx_total::14 argocd:argocd-server:80::10.0.2.4:8080::rq_active::0 argocd:argocd-server:80::10.0.2.4:8080::rq_error::14 argocd:argocd-server:80::10.0.2.4:8080::rq_success::0 argocd:argocd-server:80::10.0.2.4:8080::health_flags::healthy ``` Envoy admin cluster stats for a working backend (different node from lease holder): ``` technitium:technitium-svc:5380::10.0.1.131:5380::cx_active::6 technitium:technitium-svc:5380::10.0.1.131:5380::cx_connect_fail::0 technitium:technitium-svc:5380::10.0.1.131:5380::cx_total::14 technitium:technitium-svc:5380::10.0.1.131:5380::rq_active::0 technitium:technitium-svc:5380::10.0.1.131:5380::rq_error::0 technitium:technitium-svc:5380::10.0.1.131:5380::rq_success::67 technitium:technitium-svc:5380::10.0.1.131:5380::health_flags::healthy ``` Relevant cilium-config values: ``` routing-mode: tunnel tunnel-protocol: vxlan proxy-use-original-source-address: "true" enable-bpf-tproxy: "true" external-envoy-proxy: "true" kube-proxy-replacement: "true" gateway-api-hostnetwork-enabled: "false" bpf-lb-sock-hostns-only: "true" ``` ### Workaround Setting `proxy-use-original-source-address: "false"` in the cilium-config ConfigMap and restarting cilium + cilium-envoy DaemonSets resolves the issue. However, this cannot be done via Helm values because the chart hardcodes this to `true` when `kubeProxyReplacement: true`. ### Additional context - The issue was initially observed with technitium (DNS server) being the only pod on the control-plane node. When the L2 lease was on that node, only technitium failed. After a cilium restart moved the lease to a worker node, technitium started working but all worker-node backends broke. - `gatewayAPI.hostNetwork.enabled: true` has no effect when `external-envoy-proxy: true` (Cilium 1.20 default) - no dedicated gateway pods are created. - Related issues with similar symptoms but different root causes: #42325, #35559, #36004, #32592 ### Cilium Version 1.20.0 ### Kernel Version Linux drone-two 7.0.0-1016-raspi #16-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu Jul 23 22:56:44 UTC 2026 aarch64 GNU/Linux ### Kubernetes Version v1.36.3+k3s1 ### Regression _No response_ ### Sysdump [cilium-sysdump-20260818-144359.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31178210/cilium-sysdump-20260818-144359.zip) ### Relevant log output ```shell ``` ### Anything else? _No response_ ### Cilium Users Document - [ ] Are you a user of Cilium? Please add yourself to the [Users doc](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/USERS.md) ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

signals.title: Gateway API: intermittent fixed ~5.02s stall before request is proxied upstream (v1.19.4, VXLAN, no node encryption)
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.19.6 and lower than v1.20.0 ### What happened? # Gateway API: intermittent fixed ~5.02s stall before request is proxied upstream (v1.19.4, VXLAN, no node encryption) ## Summary Requests through a Gateway API listener intermittently stall for a fixed **~5.02 seconds** before the request is proxied to the backend. The backend never sees the request during the stall. Envoy reports no timeouts, retries, or circuit-breaker events, and there is no 5s value anywhere in the effective Envoy config. No requests are lost — with a client timeout above 5s everything completes successfully. Reproducible across four independent clusters. Rate correlates **inversely** with node count, which we cannot explain. ## Environment - Cilium **v1.19.4**, cilium-envoy **v1.36.6** - Gateway API, `kube-proxy-replacement=true` - `routing-mode=tunnel` (VXLAN), jumbo MTU (`cilium_vxlan` 9001, `cilium_wg0` 8921, physical NIC 9001) - `enable-wireguard=true` with **`NodeEncryption: Disabled`** - Managed Kubernetes on AWS, arm64 (Graviton) nodes; Amazon Linux 2023, kernel `6.12.88-119.157.amzn2023.aarch64` - Gateway fronted by an internal L4 load balancer (instance targets, cross-zone enabled, client-IP preservation on) Relevant cilium-config values (no 5s among them): ``` proxy-connect-timeout: 2 proxy-idle-timeout-seconds: 60 http-stream-idle-timeout: 300 proxy-initial-fetch-timeout: 30 gateway-api-service-externaltrafficpolicy: Cluster ``` Effective Envoy config timeouts (from `/config_dump`): `idle_timeout 60s`, `stream_idle_timeout 300s`, `connect_timeout 2s`, `initial_fetch_timeout 30s`, plus `600s`/`900s` route timeouts. **No 5s value.** ## Symptom Client is a pod in-cluster calling an HTTPS hostname routed to the internal Gateway. `curl` timing on a stalled request: ``` total=5.024006 time_appconnect=0.023203 time_starttransfer=5.023998 code=000 ``` TLS completes normally (~23ms), then nothing for ~5.0s. The stall lands at 5.02s regardless of client timeout: | Client timeout | Result | | --- | --- | | `--max-time 5` | 28/30 | | `--max-time 20` | 28/30, the 2 slow ones at **5.025s** and **5.024s** | | `--max-time 30` | **60/60 complete**, 7 slow | Raising the client timeout does not move where the stall lands, so this is not client impatience. ## The backend never receives the request during the stall Backend has a **single replica**, so the backend node is constant and only the Envoy node varies per request. `tcpdump` in the backend pod's netns, correlated with per-request timings. For a request that stalled from `02:18:48.8` to `02:18:53.9`, the backend received **zero packets** for the whole window — the next SYN to `:8080` arrives at `02:18:53.944`, i.e. only after the stall clears: ``` 02:18:48.764381 In IP <envoy-a>.46017 > <backend>.8080: Flags [S] ... 02:18:48.802412 In IP <envoy-b>.42843 > <backend>.8080: Flags [S] ... 02:18:48.838080 In IP <envoy-a>.44405 > <backend>.8080: Flags [S] ... 02:18:48.874295 In IP <envoy-c>.32887 > <backend>.8080: Flags [S] ... ... 5 SECOND GAP, nothing to the backend ... 02:18:53.944994 In IP <envoy-d>.45869 > <backend>.8080: Flags [S] ... ``` Largest inter-packet gaps on the backend side were `5.066s` and `5.056s`, matching the stalls. Client-side capture of a stalled vs a succeeding connection — byte-identical until the request, then: | | Success | Stalled | | --- | --- | --- | | request (`len 136`) sent | `39.480903` | `39.519219` | | next activity | `39.492036` (**+11ms**) | `44.518844` (**+5000ms**) | So the request is sent and ACKed at TCP level, but not proxied upstream for ~5s. ## The backend is never slow ``` cluster...<backend>_8080.upstream_rq_time: P0=4ms P50=6.0ms P90=7.1ms P99=9.1ms P100=9.1ms ``` Max upstream request time across 90 requests: **9.1ms**. ## Envoy reports no timeout of any kind Zero on all of: `upstream_rq_timeout`, `upstream_rq_retry`, `upstream_rq_per_try_timeout`, `upstream_cx_connect_timeout`, `upstream_cx_overflow`, `circuit_breakers`. No listener `downstream_cx_overflow`, no `downstream_pre_cx_timeout`, no overload-manager activity. Counters that did move over a 60-request run with 7 stalls: | Counter | Value | | --- | --- | | `upstream_cx_idle_timeout` | 44 | | `upstream_cx_destroy_local` | 44 | | `upstream_cx_total` | 47 | | `upstream_rq_per_cx` | P50=2.0 | | `downstream_cx_delayed_close_timeout` | 2 | | `upstream_rq_pending_total` | 41 → 47 | We initially suspected upstream connection-pool churn from this, but **ruled it out**: another cluster with the *lowest* stall rate (~2%) idle-reaps **100%** of its upstream connections (e.g. 103 requests over 102 connections) versus 94% here. Higher churn, lower stall rate — so aggressive idle-reaping appears to be normal behaviour and is not the mechanism. ## Only via the Gateway | Path | Result | Stalls | | --- | --- | --- | | Internal Gateway | 28/30 at 5s timeout | 2 | | k8s Service (`http://svc:8080`) | **30/30** | **0** | | Direct pod IP | **20/20** | **0** | ## Rates across four clusters (5s client timeout, so these are stall rates) | Cluster | Relative node count | Internal Gateway | External Gateway | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | A | largest (~4.5x smallest) | ~2% | 0% | | B | ~2.2x smallest | ~6% | 0% | | C | smallest | ~18% | 0% | | D | smallest | ~11% | 0% | Cilium version, cilium-envoy version, cilium-config, Gateway API config, load-balancer and target-group attributes, Envoy coverage, MTU, and pod/service CIDRs are identical across all four. **External** Gateway listeners in the same clusters are unaffected (0%). The inverse correlation with node count is consistent but unexplained. It is not a bad AZ or a bad LB node — pinning each load-balancer IP individually gives a uniform rate (2, 3, 2 stalls out of 25 each). ## Ruled out (with evidence) load-balancer target health · Gateway API config · load-balancer/target-group attributes · BPF rate limiting · connection reuse and idle timeout · ALPN · cilium datapath drops (`cilium-dbg monitor --type drop` captured 0 during a live failure) · Hubble drops · Envoy `no_filter_chain_match` · Envoy protocol errors · listen-queue overflow · node churn/age · Envoy coverage · cilium version/config differences · WireGuard · MTU · CIDR collision · client DNS (`time_namelookup` is 1.5ms on stalled requests; `ndots:5` search-path expansion investigated and excluded) · `wireguard-persistent-keepalive=0s` (stalls persist under continuous back-to-back load, including consecutive stalls) · upstream connection-pool churn (see above) · TCP RSTs observed in-pod (they appear on successful requests too — ordinary client teardown) ## Notes on related issues - #40428 (v1.18 hardcoded 5s `connectTimeout`) — fix shipped in v1.19.0; we are on v1.19.4 and our `connect_timeout` is `2s`, so this is not it. - #32592 — we already run `encryption.enabled: true` + `encryption.type: wireguard`, the workaround reported there, and still stall. That report is hostNetwork + VPC-CNI chaining with 100% cross-node failure; ours is intermittent, no hostNetwork. - #46100 — enabling `encryption.nodeEncryption: true` on one cluster took our stall rate from ~12% to **100%**, matching #46100's conditions (VXLAN + node encryption, NIC MTU 9000, `wg0` 8921, v1.19.3+). We reverted. Note this is a **separate** problem: with node encryption disabled we see **no fragmentation drops at all** (`cilium_ipv4_frag_datagrams` untouched, no `DROP_FRAG_NOT_FOUND`), yet the ~12% stall persists. ## What would help Any pointer to what, in the Gateway API path, could defer proxying an already-accepted request by a fixed ~5s without incrementing any Envoy timeout counter. We are happy to run further captures or provide a sysdump. ### How can we reproduce the issue? ## Reproduction / methods used Packet capture inside a pod (streaming via `kubectl debug -it` was unreliable for us; write to a file and read via `kubectl logs`): ```bash kubectl -n <ns> debug <pod> --image=nicolaka/netshoot:latest --target=<container> -q -- \ bash -c 'tcpdump -i any -nn -S -tttt "tcp port 443" > /tmp/c.txt & sleep 3; <drive traffic>; kill -INT %1; <analyse>' kubectl -n <ns> logs <pod> -c <debugger-name> ``` Envoy admin stats from a node (no curl in the envoy/agent images): ```bash curl -s --unix-socket /var/run/cilium/envoy/sockets/admin.sock http://localhost/stats ``` The Envoy listener port for a Gateway changes on reconfiguration — read it from `/listeners` rather than hardcoding. ### Cilium Version **Environment** - Cilium `v1.19.4`, cilium-envoy `v1.36.6` - `routing-mode=tunnel` (VXLAN), `kube-proxy-replacement=true` - Managed Kubernetes on AWS, **arm64** (Graviton) nodes - Jumbo frames: physical NIC `9001`, `cilium_vxlan` `9001`, `cilium_wg0` **`8921`** ### Kernel Version - Amazon Linux 2023, kernel `6.12.88-119.157.amzn2023.aarch64` ### Kubernetes Version - Managed Kubernetes 1.35 on AWS, **arm64** (Graviton) nodes ### Regression _No response_ ### Sysdump _No response_ ### Relevant log output ```shell ``` ### Anything else? _No response_ ### Cilium Users Document - [ ] Are you a user of Cilium? Please add yourself to the [Users doc](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/USERS.md) ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

signals.title: Host firewall: policy-selected node is permanently isolated after reboot — host endpoint policy map ends up deny-all (cold boot, audit-off flip) or allow-all (runtime label add), never the computed policy
signals.text: ## Is there an existing issue for this? Closest match is #25448 ("host firewall drops reply traffic for legitimate connections when policies are first enforced"). This report is a stronger manifestation of what looks like the same enforcement-transition problem: in our setup the drop window is not transient — it is fatal and self-sustaining (node permanently isolated until out-of-band reboot), it reproduces on every cold boot, and it also reproduces on a fully synced agent when audit mode is switched off at runtime. Filing separately because the evidence points at the host endpoint's BPF policy map never receiving the computed allow entries, with three distinct end states depending on the path taken. ## What happened? Environment: Cilium 1.18.6 (kubespray), host firewall enabled, kube-proxy replacement enabled, VXLAN tunnel, WireGuard node encryption, `bpf-datapath-mode: netkit`, CRD identity mode, 61 nodes. A `CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy` with `nodeSelector` on worker nodes provides ingress lock-down (fromEntities cluster/remote-node/health/host, SSH/ICMP via CiliumCIDRGroup refs plus literal CIDRs, kubelet/NodePort from cluster). **1. Cold boot of a selected node → permanent isolation.** ~13 s after cilium-agent starts, every packet in and out is dropped as `Policy denied` by `bpf_host.c:865`. The node never recovers: the agent needs the apiserver to finish its sync, and its own egress to the apiserver is what is being dropped. Captured from inside a locked node (systemd unit dumping via crictl exec): - at agent start, `cilium-dbg endpoint list` is still **empty** (host endpoint not created yet) while bpf_host is already attached and enforcing deny-by-default with an empty policy map; - 105 659 `Policy denied` drops in 20 s, 73 018 of them the node's own egress to the apiserver LB: `identity host->unknown: <node-ip>:* -> <apiserver-lb-ip>:6443`; - at that moment the BPF ipcache is fully populated (8 292 entries) and local CIDR identities for the policy's allowed CIDRs are already allocated — e.g. ICMP from an explicitly allowed CIDR is dropped with its allocated identity (`identity 16777222->unknown`). The policy is computed; its allow entries are just not in the host endpoint policy map. **2. Runtime audit-off flip on a fully synced agent → same isolation.** Boot the node with `policy-audit-mode: true` (per-node CiliumNodeConfig): node comes up healthy, host endpoint reaches `state=ready`, realized policy has all 8 L4 ingress rules, `enforcement=audit-ingress`. Then `cilium-dbg endpoint config <hostep> PolicyAuditMode=Disabled` → "configuration updated successfully" → the node is fully isolated within seconds. The agent log ends abruptly mid incremental `UpdatePolicyMaps` processing with no error line — consistent with the deny default being installed while the allow entries never land. **3. Warm enforcement via label add → policy map silently allow-all.** With the agent fully synced and the node label added at runtime (CCNP starts selecting the node), the endpoint reports `enforcement=ingress`, but `cilium-dbg bpf policy get <hostep>` contains only the wildcard pair (`Allow Ingress ANY` prefix 0 / `Allow Egress ANY` prefix 0) — i.e. no actual enforcement. This is the only transition that leaves the node reachable, and it appears to do so by not programming the policy at all. For contrast, a long-running node whose agent processed the CCNP incrementally while already enforcing has a fully programmed map (per-identity allows, port ranges) — so the policy→map pipeline itself works. So the same policy, same version, produces three different host endpoint policy-map end states depending on the transition path: deny-all (cold boot, audit-off flip), allow-all (runtime label add), correct (incremental update on an already-enforcing endpoint). Datapath mode does not appear to matter: a cold boot with `bpf-datapath-mode: veth` (per-node CiliumNodeConfig) locked out identically (caveat: the override's application could not be positively confirmed from inside the locked node). Impact: any reboot of a policy-selected node isolates it permanently; recovery requires out-of-band console/rescue access. 54 nodes affected in our cluster. ## Cilium Version 1.18.6 ## Kernel Version 6.8.0-124-generic (Ubuntu 24.04) ## Kubernetes Version v1.33.7 (kubespray) ## Sysdump Not attached (production cluster); can provide targeted captures on request. Full monitor drop capture (17 MB) and repeated boot-time snapshots of `endpoint list` / `bpf policy get` / `bpf ipcache list` from inside a locked node are preserved. ## Relevant log output ``` xx drop (Policy denied) flow 0x... to endpoint 0, ifindex 7, file bpf_host.c:865, , identity host->unknown: <node-ip>:39186 -> <apiserver-lb-ip>:6443 tcp SYN xx drop (Policy denied) flow 0x... to endpoint 0, ifindex 2, file bpf_host.c:865, , identity 16777222->unknown: <allowed-admin-ip> -> <node-ip> icmp EchoRequest ``` Agent start with audit mode (the boot that survives): ``` level=warn msg="PolicyAuditMode is enabled. Network policy will not be enforced." level=info msg="Regenerating restored endpoints" restored=0 level=info msg="Creating host endpoint" ``` ## Anything else? - The reboot lockout window matches #25448's "first enforcement" semantics; unlike #25448 the state is permanent because the dropped traffic includes the agent's own apiserver path (chicken-and-egg). - Feature combination overlaps with #31209 (tunnel + KPR + WireGuard + host firewall). - Nothing relevant found in 1.18.7–1.18.13 changelogs. - Happy to run instrumented builds / additional captures on a dedicated test node. ## Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

signals.title: gateway-api: an apiserver 500 during CRD discovery is treated as "CRDs not installed", disabling Gateway API for the lifetime of the operator
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.19.6 and lower than v1.20.0 ### What happened? Follow-up to #43130 (fixed by #43452 and #44662). Those fixes handle the case where the apiserver is unreachable at the network level. This report is about the remaining hole: an apiserver that answers, but answers 500. `cilium-operator` started while etcd was going through a leader election. The Gateway API CRD discovery GET came back as a server-side error, the operator logged the "resources are not found" message and moved on with Gateway API off. No retry, no backoff warning, no restart. The pod then ran for two hours without a single further gateway-related log line, and the GatewayClass kept the default `Accepted=Unknown / Pending / "Waiting for controller"` status that the upstream CRD ships. Deleting the operator pod fixed it immediately. The CRDs were installed the whole time. The operator said they were not. Expected: a transient server-side failure is retried like a transient network failure, and if it does not clear, the operator exits so the kubelet restarts it. Only a real "the CRD is absent" answer should disable Gateway API silently. ### Mechanism `discoverCRDsWithRetry` splits every discovery failure into "retry" and "the CRDs are not installed" using `isTransientError`, and the second branch is the default: - https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/ee26050851a92746155a7319b2554054adb0966c/operator/pkg/gateway-api/cell.go#L162-L169 - https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/ee26050851a92746155a7319b2554054adb0966c/operator/pkg/gateway-api/cell.go#L365-L388 `isTransientError` is an allowlist: four `k8serrors` predicates (`IsServerTimeout`, `IsServiceUnavailable`, `IsTooManyRequests`, `IsTimeout`) plus four `syscall.Errno` values. A 500 carrying `Reason: InternalError` matches none of them, and that is exactly what the apiserver returns when the storage layer fails: `Internal error occurred: etcdserver: leader changed`. Neither does a bare 500 with no reason (`IsUnexpectedServerError`), nor a transport error that is not a plain `syscall.Errno`, such as `http2: client connection lost` or a `Client.Timeout` wrapped in `*url.Error`. Nothing upstream of that narrows it either. `checkCRDs` joins raw client errors, and `CheckCRD` returns the client error untouched; `NotFound` is never distinguished from anything else: - https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/ee26050851a92746155a7319b2554054adb0966c/pkg/k8s/client/crd.go#L15-L37 So the branch that is supposed to mean "the operator looked and the CRD is genuinely absent" is reached by every failure mode the allowlist does not name, and its effect is permanent: `Enabled: false` is returned to the hive, `registerReconcilers` never runs, and no watch, timer or health probe re-enters the path. v1.19 is the same code, verified on the v1.19.7 tag: https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/44d55ea770e38bdf4b3a5f5d8079ab311f5a4911/operator/pkg/gateway-api/cell.go#L170-L177 ### Impact Any cluster where the control plane can return a server-side error for a second or two at operator startup. Managed and self-hosted control planes move etcd leadership during upgrades, node replacement and maintenance; the operator is restarted at exactly those moments. The failure is silent — the operator is Running and Ready, the message points at installation docs for CRDs that are already installed, and nothing recovers without a manual pod delete. ### Suggested fix Invert the default. Retry unless the error is specifically `k8serrors.IsNotFound`, i.e. treat "the CRD object does not exist" as the only permanent answer and everything else as retryable. That also removes the need to keep extending the allowlist for every new error shape. If the allowlist stays, it needs at least `IsInternalError` and `IsUnexpectedServerError`, plus a `net.Error` check for transport errors that do not carry an `Errno`. Either way the message on the permanent branch should be reworded: "resources are not found" is what sent me to check the CRDs first, and they were fine. ### How can we reproduce the issue? 1. Install the Gateway API CRDs and enable `gatewayAPI.enabled=true`. 2. Make the apiserver return 500 for `GET /apis/apiextensions.k8s.io/v1/customresourcedefinitions/gatewayclasses.gateway.networking.k8s.io` for a few seconds during operator startup. Losing the etcd leader is the natural way; an admission webhook or a proxy that injects 500 works too. 3. Start `cilium-operator` into that window. 4. `kubectl get gatewayclass cilium -o yaml` stays at `Accepted=Unknown`, and the operator log has exactly one gateway line after the discovery message. It never recovers. ### Cilium Version v1.19.5 (vendored chart; behavior verified identical on the v1.19.7 tag) ### Kernel Version 6.18.38 (Talos v1.13.6) ### Kubernetes Version v1.35.6 ### Regression _No response_ ### Sysdump _No response_ ### Relevant log output ```shell level=info msg="Checking for required and optional GatewayAPI resources" requiredGVK="[gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1, Kind=gatewayclasses ...]" level=error msg="Required GatewayAPI resources are not found, please refer to docs for installation instructions" error="etcdserver: leader changed" The absence of the `"Failed to check GatewayAPI CRDs due to transient error, will retry"` warning is the tell: the backoff loop was never entered, the error went straight down the permanent branch on the first attempt. ``` ### Anything else? _No response_ ### Cilium Users Document - [ ] Are you a user of Cilium? Please add yourself to the [Users doc](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/USERS.md) ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

signals.title: l2announcer: leader-election Lease name is a plain namespace+name concatenation, so two Services can end up sharing one Lease
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.19.6 and lower than v1.20.0 ### What happened? L2 announcements derive the per-Service leader-election Lease name by gluing the namespace and the Service name onto a prefix with a hyphen, and a hyphen is legal inside both halves. Two unrelated Services can therefore map onto the same Lease name and end up in one leader election. ```go const leasePrefix = "cilium-l2announce" Name: fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s-%s", leasePrefix, svc.Name.Namespace(), svc.Name.Name()), ``` https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/ee26050851a92746155a7319b2554054adb0966c/pkg/l2announcer/l2announcer.go#L847-L860 Namespace `foo` + Service `bar-baz`, and namespace `foo-bar` + Service `baz`, both produce `cilium-l2announce-foo-bar-baz`. There is no sanitization, escaping or hashing anywhere on that path; the only other place the name is touched is the GC scan, which just prefix-matches (`strings.HasPrefix(lease.Name, leasePrefix)`) and does not disambiguate either. Same code on v1.19: https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/44d55ea770e38bdf4b3a5f5d8079ab311f5a4911/pkg/l2announcer/l2announcer.go#L820-L826 Expected: one Lease per Service. ### Mechanism ### Impact Needs a hyphen in the right place, so it is not going to be common, but it is silent when it happens and the symptom points at the L2 policy rather than at a name collision. Multi-tenant clusters where namespaces are generated with a prefix (`team-a`, `team-a-staging`) and Service names are equally hyphenated are where I would expect it. ### Suggested fix Use a separator that cannot appear in either half. Neither a namespace (DNS-1123 label) nor a Service name (DNS-1035 label) may contain `.`, and `.` is legal in an object name (DNS-1123 subdomain), so `fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s.%s", leasePrefix, ns, name)` is unambiguous and stays readable in `kubectl get leases`. A hash suffix would also work but costs readability. Either way the name changes on upgrade, which orphans the existing Leases. Those are released on agent shutdown (`ReleaseOnCancel`), which empties the holder identity, and `leaseGC` already deletes prefix-matching Leases with an empty holder, so the old objects should clean themselves up. I have not confirmed that. ### How can we reproduce the issue? 1. Enable L2 announcements and a `CiliumLoadBalancerIPPool`. 2. `kubectl create namespace foo && kubectl create namespace foo-bar` 3. Create Service `bar-baz` of type LoadBalancer in `foo`, and Service `baz` of type LoadBalancer in `foo-bar`. 4. Create `CiliumL2AnnouncementPolicy` objects selecting both, with disjoint `nodeSelector`s so the two Services are announced from different nodes. 5. `kubectl get leases -n kube-system | grep cilium-l2announce` shows one Lease named `cilium-l2announce-foo-bar-baz` instead of two. ### Cilium Version N/A — found by source inspection, no live cluster involved. ### Kernel Version N/A — found by source inspection, no live cluster involved. ### Kubernetes Version N/A — found by source inspection, no live cluster involved. ### Regression _No response_ ### Sysdump _No response_ ### Relevant log output ```shell ``` ### Anything else? _No response_ ### Cilium Users Document - [ ] Are you a user of Cilium? Please add yourself to the [Users doc](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/USERS.md) ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

signals.title: CFP: Support dynamic IP address allocation in Cilium Network Driver
signals.text: ### Is your proposed feature related to a problem? The Cilium Network Driver proposed in [cilium/cilium#43295](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/43295) and [CFP-43295](https://github.com/cilium/design-cfps/pull/85) can allocate and prepare network devices for Pods through Kubernetes Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA). Those devices may also need IPv4 and/or IPv6 addresses, but the Network Driver does not have a scalable way to allocate them dynamically. Requiring a cluster operator to assign static addresses does not scale and is particularly unsafe with reusable `ResourceClaimTemplate` objects: multiple claims created from the same template must not receive the same address. Cilium Pod IPAM modes cannot be used directly because these addresses belong to claimed network resources, not to the Pod's primary Cilium interface, and their allocation lifecycle follows DRA prepare/unprepare operations rather than CNI endpoint creation and deletion. Without dedicated resource IPAM, operators must maintain per-workload address assignments themselves, cannot safely reuse claim templates, and cannot independently manage address capacity for different secondary networks or device classes. ### Describe the feature you'd like Add dedicated IPAM support for the Cilium Network Driver. It should manage addresses for DRA network resources and coexist with any IPAM mode used for Pods; enabling it must not change or consume capacity from Pod IPAM. ### Requirements - Support IPv4-only, IPv6-only, and dual-stack configurations. Allow cluster operators to define the address spaces available to DRA resources, including efficient use of small address ranges. - Support independently managed address spaces for different secondary networks or device classes, and allow each DRA device request to identify its intended address space. Cilium must not silently allocate an address from a different network when the requested address space is unavailable. - Allocate the required address or addresses while preparing a DRA `ResourceClaim`, before the device is configured for the Pod. The allocated addresses must be exposed through the claim's allocated-device status so that the result is inspectable and can be restored. - Make claim operations idempotent. Retrying preparation must preserve the existing allocation rather than consume another address. Cilium component restarts must not change live allocations, and a partially failed preparation must roll back any newly allocated addresses. - Release addresses when the claim is unprepared and they are no longer used. Stale capacity must be reclaimed safely when nodes or claims disappear. - Handle concurrent claims without duplicate live allocations within the same address space. Missing configuration, address-family mismatches, and exhaustion must leave the claim unprepared and surface an actionable, retryable error. - Scale across large node counts and high claim churn without allocation latency or API-server and control-plane load becoming a bottleneck. Unused capacity must be reclaimable safely. - Cover the allocation, retry, restart/restore, rollback, release, exhaustion, IPv4, IPv6, and dual-stack paths with automated tests and document the operational lifecycle. ### Scope and non-goals This issue is limited to IP address management for network devices handled by the Cilium Network Driver. It does not propose changes to device discovery, DRA scheduling, SR-IOV or other device-manager behavior, VLAN or route configuration, NRI integration, or Cilium datapath connectivity for the secondary interface. It also does not replace existing Pod IPAM modes or track static address assignment. ### Notify relevant community channels @cilium/network-driver @cilium/sig-ipam

signals.title: gateway-api: same-port HTTPS and TLS passthrough listeners are rejected on any SNI overlap, including a wildcard HTTPS listener next to an exact passthrough hostname
signals.text: ### Is your proposed feature related to a problem? Since v1.19.6 / v1.20.0, an HTTPS/Terminate listener and a TLS/Passthrough listener on the same port are marked `Conflicted=True/ProtocolConflict` whenever their hostnames intersect (`listenerPairConflict` on main, `samePortCrossProtocolConflictedListeners` on v1.19). So `*.example.com` (HTTPS) next to `api.example.com` (TLS passthrough) on 443 gets both listeners `Accepted=False`, and on 1.20 both are dropped from Envoy (#47306, #47457). This worked up to v1.19.5, so for the v1.19 branch it is also a regression: a config that 1.19.5 accepted and served stopped being accepted in the 1.19.6 patch release. #32292 is the same shape (`*.test` HTTPS + `proxmox.test` passthrough on 443), reproduced by a maintainer and accepted, and Envoy picks the exact `server_names` chain over the wildcard one. What actually broke was two listeners with the same hostname (two filter chains with the same match). The #44889 review asked to reject that same-hostname pair; the intersect predicate also caught the wildcard-superset case, and nothing tested it: the scenario matrix has same-port disjoint hostnames (works) and same-port same hostname (rejected), nothing in between. #47590 hit it on 1.20.0 and was closed after the reporter withdrew, so it was never discussed on its own. Why I care (Cozystack, cozystack/cozystack#3912): one Gateway with one address per tenant; on 443 a wildcard `*.<apex>` HTTPS listener for apps plus passthrough listeners for `api.<apex>` (management kube-apiserver, passthrough so clients see the real cert), `vm-exportproxy.<apex>` and `cdi-uploadproxy.<apex>`. One address per tenant is a hard constraint (every Gateway wants 443, so LB-IPAM sharing is out), and `api.<apex>:443` is in every kubeconfig. With the intersect rule we have to drop the wildcard and render one HTTPS listener per hostname under the 64-listener cap. Works, but a wildcard next to a more specific listener is exactly what the spec's hostname precedence rule is for. ### Describe the feature you'd like Conflict a same-port HTTPS/Terminate + TLS/Passthrough pair only when the normalized hostnames are equal (both catch-all included), the case Envoy can't disambiguate. For a strict wildcard superset (`*.example.com` vs `api.example.com`) apply the spec's "exact matches MUST be processed before wildcard matches" and accept both, as two HTTPS listeners with those hostnames on one port are accepted today. That keeps the #44889 same-hostname rejection and makes the cross-protocol branch match the same-protocol one. The spec lets an implementation call HTTPS and TLS on one port incompatible, so against the spec this is a request, not a conformance bug. Against v1.19 it is a regression fix, so I'd also ask for a backport there. Cilium already mixes the two protocols on one port for disjoint hostnames, and Envoy expresses the precedence. ### Notify relevant community channels @cilium/sig-servicemesh ### (Optional) Describe your proposed solution In `listenerPairConflict` (`operator/pkg/gateway-api/gateway_reconcile.go`; `listenersHaveSamePortCrossProtocolHostnameConflict` on v1.19/v1.20): conflict when `normalizedListenerHostname(first) == normalizedListenerHostname(second)`, otherwise not, same as the same-protocol branch below it. Translation already emits both filter chains on one listener and the matcher picks the exact server name first. Plus a test scenario for same port, wildcard HTTPS, exact passthrough, traffic to both names, and a re-check of `tlsroute-mixed-protocol-listeners`. I can do the PR if you want it; I'd rather agree on the rule here first.
