signal.title: WireGuard node-to-node encryption: oversized packets cause fragmentation, and BPF fragment tracking drops most second fragments
signal.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.19.3 and lower than v1.20.0 ### What happened? We identified two seemingly related issues when using Cilium's WireGuard-based node-to-node encryption with host-network pods on nodes. 1. WireGuard encapsulation produces packets exceeding the physical NIC MTU, causing IP fragmentation that should not occur. This is related to https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/23917 and _might_ be addressed by https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/45940. However when artificially setting the cilium_wg0 interface MTU to a lower value, the issue does not disappear completely, suggesting traffic originating on the node's interface (host-network pods) might not really benefit from it. I plan to revisit this after I'm able to test the above official fix. 2. Most second fragments are dropped by Cilium's BPF TC ingress program with DROP_FRAG_NOT_FOUND ("First logical datagram fragment not found"). edit: after digging a bit more, I wouldn't be surprised if this was just caused by a simple out-of-order reassembly, which doesn't seem supported yet https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/25709#issuecomment-1969602232 As a hacky workaround, setting the WG interface MTU to 9000-95, PLUS clamping TCP connections on the physical NIC to 9000-95-40 prevents fragmented packets and seems it resolve both issues (only for TCP). ### How can we reproduce the issue? Cloud provider: OCI (Oracle Cloud Infrastructure) Datapath mode: VXLAN tunnel + WireGuard encryption with Node encryption enabled Physical NIC MTU: 9000 Host-network pods: yes (both sides of the connection) Establish a normal TCP connection between the 2 pods, sending relevant amount of data. signal.title: bpf: migrate non-branching config macros to runtime configuration
signal.text: The current step in the clang-freedom (pre-compiled eBPF programs) journey is to start transitioning compile time configuration to load-time (runtime) configuration. The necessary agent and loader infrastructure has been merged. Runtime configuration can be defined with [`DECLARE_CONFIG` and `NODE_CONFIG`](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/bpf/lib/static_data.h). See [Configuring the Datapath](https://docs.cilium.io/en/latest/contributing/development/datapath_config) in the Cilium Developer docs for guidelines and principles. ~~This issue specifically tracks variables which do not influence control flow by enabling or disabling certain code paths. Variables used in `#ifdef`/`#if` and `if(is_defined(...))` will be converted in 1.19 since dead code elimination only really landed in Linux 5.5, and Cilium 1.18 targets Linux 5.4 which will go EOL at the end of 2025.~~ 1.19 targets Linux 5.10. We can migrate branching macros, too. Additionally, https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/41628 shipped in 1.19 which added dead code detection in the agent to avoid loading unused maps and tail calls. Branching macros can now safely be ported. This issue is for migrating `node_config.h` and `WriteNodeConfig` entries to `config.Node`, as well as some leftover per-object configs in `ep_config.h`. Through this issue, we can coordinate work and keep an overview. If you want to work on a particular (set of) variable(s), drop a comment and we'll spin out an issue or assign you to a list item. The list may change over time and may grow as we find more work in this category. signal.title: api: Type the MAC fields as `mac.MAC`
signal.text: The five MAC fields in the agent API were plain strings that every consumer immediately parsed. This PR types them with `x-go-type`, the same way 99d9d398fc did for `Address` and `CIDR`, so the model carries the semantic type and the round-trip noise disappears. There are also two setup commits to help with that: one making `pkg/mac` a leaf package, so that `api/v1/models` can import it without dragging in netlink and k8s dependencies, and another commit typing `ipam.AllocationResult.PrimaryMAC` so the master interface MAC is parsed once on entry rather than on every use. See the individual commits message for details.

signal.title: cli: ignore ENI IPv6 beta warning and detect IPv6 EKS server URL
signal.text: # Ignoring the beta warning The ENI IPv6 implementation is in beta for the v1.20 release of Cilium. This adds the beta warning log to the list of expected warnings in the CLI. Otherwise, the error check test fails when running connectivity tests with ENI+IPv6 enabled. Example test error: ``` . ❌ Found 1 logs in [...]/my-ipv6-cluster/kube-system/cilium-operator-b8c85f56b-txldk (cilium-operator) matching list of errors that must be investigated: time=2026-07-27T15:48:15.96359495Z level=warn msg="IPv6 support in the ENI IPAM mode (ipam.mode=eni, ipv6.enabled=true) is a beta feature. Please use it with caution and report any issues you encounter: https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/new?template=bug_report.yaml" subsys=cilium-operator-aws (1 occurrences) ``` The error no longer appears after this change. # Detecting EKS IPv6 server URL For IPv6 EKS clusters, the format of the server URL is different than that of IPv4 clusters. For IPv6, the URL is suffixed with eks-cluster.\<region\>.api.aws (See https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/cluster-endpoint.html#cluster-endpoint-ipv6). This change relaxes detection of EKS flavor by server endpoint URL. The new condition should match all types of EKS clusters (Commercial, GovCloud, China) (IPv4, IPv6). However, I did note some inconsistencies in the AWS docs as in IPv4 I get this pattern `https://ABCDEF1234567890.gr7.us-west-2.eks.amazonaws.com` while on IPv6 I get the `eks-cluster` substring `https://ABCDEF1234567890.gr7.eks-cluster.us-west-2.api.aws`. I'm not sure if we get either the `.eks-cluster.` or `.eks.` substrings in China and I can't test it myself. ```release-note cli: the CLI now considers the ENI IPv6 beta warning log as expected and detects EKS flavor for IPv6 EKS clusters. ```

signal.text: - [ ] For first time contributors, read [Submitting a pull request] - [ ] All code is covered by unit and/or runtime tests where feasible. - [x] All commits contain a well written commit description including a title, description and a `Fixes: #XXX` line if the commit addresses a particular GitHub issue. - [ ] If your commit description contains a `Fixes: <commit-id>` tag, then please add the commit author[s] as reviewer[s] to this issue. - [x] All commits are signed off. See the section [Developer’s Certificate of Origin] - [x] Provide a title or release-note blurb suitable for the release notes. - [ ] Disclose use of machine learning models (including LLMs and other generative AI) in accordance with the [Cilium AI Policy], and indicate the rating using [AI Influence Level]. Example: "This PR was prepared with AIL:3. I personally checked X." - [x] Thanks for contributing! <!-- TODO(me): add my own AI disclosure sentence and tick the box above. --> The chart rendered `prometheus.io/scrape` and `prometheus.io/port` as literal lines next to the user's own annotation map, so setting either key produced a duplicate YAML key and precedence came down to render order. The chart default is rendered last for `hubble-metrics`, the `hubble-relay` Service and the `hubble-relay` pod, so those three silently discarded the user value, which is why annotation-based scraping could not be turned off. Both keys now render through a helper that skips the ones the user already set. Each key appears once and the user value always wins, so `prometheus.io/scrape: "false"` keeps the metrics port exposed while opting out of annotation-based scraping. No new Helm values are added. Verified with `helm template` across the default, metrics-enabled, override, ServiceMonitor and embedded-Envoy paths: default output is unchanged apart from key ordering, and no manifest carries a duplicate key. ```release-note Helm: user-supplied annotations now take precedence over the chart's prometheus.io/scrape and prometheus.io/port annotations, which no longer render as duplicate keys. ``` AIL:1 Fixes: #47821

signal.title: bpf: ICMP checksum handling in SNAT RevNAT
signal.text:
Fixes: https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/40827 When a LB node forwards packets to a backend-pod on another node, the packets are SNATed. The corresponding reverse NAT (RevNAT) is then applied to the reply packets. Checksum recaluculation is required when RevNAT. When the reply packet is an ICMP error packet, the checksum in the ICMP header must be recalculated to reflect the changes of the inner packet header. https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5508#section-4.1 Since that logic was missing, it has been added in this commit. The below is an error message of `nat4_icmp_error_tcp_snat_revnat` ([new test](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43196/commits/c4fff34f4e484af5328add58afff0f007a0ad002)) without the [checksum recalculate patch](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43196/commits/8495c0c5c063e2bd8c896e74f7d636f69666d18f).
An error message of RevNAT BPF-test ``` --- FAIL: TestBPF (39.66s) --- FAIL: TestBPF/icmp_error_revnat.o (0.55s) --- FAIL: TestBPF/icmp_error_revnat.o/nat4_icmp_error_tcp_snat_revnat (0.42s) bpf_test.go:577: icmp_error_revnat.c:137: CTX and buffer 'ICMP4_ERR_FRAG_NEEDED_AFTER_REVNAT' content mismatch bpf_test.go:421: Scapy asserts failed: 1 bpf_test.go:428: === START ./scapy.h:171 'icmp4_revnat_ok' === >>> Expected (len: 164 bytes) <<< ###[ Ethernet ]### dst = 13:37:13:37:13:37 src = de:ad:be:ef:de:ef type = IPv4 ###[ IP ]### version = 4 ihl = 5 tos = 0x0 len = 68 id = 1 flags = frag = 0 ttl = 64 proto = icmp chksum = 0xa60d src = 192.168.0.2 dst = 10.0.10.1 \options \ ###[ ICMP ]### type = dest-unreach code = fragmentation-needed chksum = 0xcbe5 reserved = 0 length = 0 nexthopmtu= 1500 unused = '' ###[ IP in ICMP ]### version = 4 ihl = 5 tos = 0x0 len = 40 id = 1 flags = DF frag = 0 ttl = 64 proto = tcp chksum = 0x6624 src = 10.0.10.1 dst = 192.168.0.2 \options \ ###[ TCP in ICMP ]### sport = 3030 dport = http seq = 0 ack = 0 dataofs = 5 reserved = 0 flags = S window = 8192 chksum = 0xaf11 urgptr = 0 options = '' >>> Got (len: 164 bytes) <<< ###[ Ethernet ]### dst = 13:37:13:37:13:37 src = de:ad:be:ef:de:ef type = IPv4 ###[ IP ]### version = 4 ihl = 5 tos = 0x0 len = 68 id = 1 flags = frag = 0 ttl = 64 proto = icmp chksum = 0xa60d src = 192.168.0.2 dst = 10.0.10.1 \options \ ###[ ICMP ]### type = dest-unreach code = fragmentation-needed chksum = 0x788e reserved = 0 length = 0 nexthopmtu= 1500 unused = '' ###[ IP in ICMP ]### version = 4 ihl = 5 tos = 0x0 len = 40 id = 1 flags = DF frag = 0 ttl = 64 proto = tcp chksum = 0x6624 src = 10.0.10.1 dst = 192.168.0.2 \options \ ###[ TCP in ICMP ]### sport = 3030 dport = http seq = 0 ack = 0 dataofs = 5 reserved = 0 flags = S window = 8192 chksum = 0xaf11 urgptr = 0 options = '' >>> Diff <<< --- a/pkt (Expected) +++ b/pkt (Got) - [ Ether ][ IP ][ ICMP ].chksum: 52197 + [ Ether ][ IP ][ ICMP ].chksum: 30862 === END ./scapy.h:171 'icmp4_revnat_ok' === ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ STATUS │ ELAPSED │ PACKAGE │ COVER │ PASS │ FAIL │ SKIP │ │─────────┼─────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────┼──────┼──────┼───────│ │ FAIL │ 39.70s │ github.com/cilium/cilium/bpf/tests/bpftest │ -- │ 594 │ 3 │ 0 │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ```

signal.title: bpf: dsr: fix outer SrcIP in ICMP error msg
signal.text: By the time that we check whether a DSR request exceeds the MTU (and respond with an ICMP error msg), the request has already been DNATed to the backend IP/port (when using "opt" or "geneve" dispatch). We are currently RevNATing only the inner headers (the original request) - but the outer IP header still uses the backend's IP as sourceIP. Instead of fixing this up manually, split the code into two stages 1. RevNAT of the rejected DSR request, and then 2. use generate_icmp*_reply() to produce the ICMP msg, replacing all the custom rewrite logic. Note that for IPIP the request is in its original form at this point, and doesn't require any RevNAT processing. ```release-note When using DSR with --bpf-lb-dsr-dispatch set to "opt" or "geneve" in combination with --enable-pmtu-discovery, fix the outer source IP of the ICMP error message which is generated when a forwarded DSR request exceeds the network interface's MTU. ```

signal.title: install: detect GKE from kubelet path
signal.text: GKE `1.36.2-gke.2064000` no longer exposes the container runtime endpoint through the `--container-runtime-endpoint` flag in `/etc/default/kubelet`. This causes the existing node-init GKE detection to miss the GKE-specific path and fall through to generic kubelet handling. Instead of detecting individual GKE node layouts through container runtime configuration, this change uses the presence of `/home/kubernetes/bin/kubelet`, which is shared by both the legacy and current GKE layouts. The same detection is used by startup and prestop, so the kubelet wrapper installed during startup can also be detected and reverted correctly. Testing performed: * `helm lint` * Helm template rendering with GKE/node-init values * `bash -n` on rendered startup and prestop scripts * sandboxed scenarios covering legacy GKE, the GKE 1.36.2 layout, generic non-GKE nodes, and an already-installed kubelet wrapper * live GKE `1.36.2-gke.2064000` COS/containerd node verification: * `/home/kubernetes/bin/kubelet` exists as a regular executable file * `/home/kubernetes/kubelet-config.yaml` contains `containerRuntimeEndpoint: unix:///run/containerd/containerd.sock` * `/etc/default/kubelet` does not contain `--container-runtime-endpoint` * `git diff --check` Claude was used to suggest the implementation. I manually reviewed the changes and validated the resulting behavior with the tests above. AIL:4 Fixes: #47884 ```release-note Fix node-init startup on GKE 1.36.2-gke.2064000 nodes by detecting GKE from the kubelet path instead of container runtime configuration. ```

signal.title: bgp: gate BGP announcements on host datapath init
signal.text: ## Description The BGP Control Plane controller starts reconciling as soon as the CiliumNode resource becomes available, which happens before `bpf_host.c` has been attached to native devices. On node reboot, this caused a "No route to host" window: the upstream router added the node back to its ECMP group, but incoming LB traffic arrived on native devices with no BPF program to DNAT it. Fix by blocking `Run()` on `Loader.HostDatapathInitialized()` before entering the event loop. The channel is closed by `ReloadDatapath()` once the host endpoint BPF programs have been attached. `Loader` is already available in the Hive dependency graph and is injected via `ControllerParams`. ## Reproduction **Setup** - Two nodes acting as BGP ECMP peers for a LoadBalancer service (`externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster`) - Upstream router distributes traffic across both nodes via ECMP - Build Cilium with a `time.Sleep(30 * time.Second)` added at the top of `ReloadDatapath()` in `pkg/datapath/loader/endpoint.go`, and deploy the modified image as the cilium-agent on both nodes **Steps to reproduce** 1. Reboot one of the two nodes 2. Send requests to the LoadBalancer VIP from an external client during the 30-second window after the rebooted node's BGP session re-establishes **Observed behavior** "No route to host" errors occur during the window. Depending on which ECMP bucket the client's 5-tuple hashes to, the failure rate should be either 100% or 0% per flow. **Expected behavior** No errors: BGP should not advertise routes until BPF programs are attached to native devices. ```release-note Fix a "No route to host" window on node reboot where BGP advertised routes before BPF programs were attached to native devices. ``` This PR was prepared with AIL:3. I personally checked the datapath attachment sequence and the HostDatapathInitialized channel lifecycle.
signal.author: tkna

signal.title: MTU issue for large UDP packets with native routing and DSR
signal.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues: this is very similar to #32601 ### Version equal or higher than v1.17.4 and lower than v1.18.0 ### What happened? The situation is almost the same as the one in the other issue: I have an environment with native routing and DSR, with a UDP (SIP) service with 3 endpoints running on 3 different nodes. There are some large (>2000) UDP packets being sent from outside the cluster to one of the endpoint, which get correctly fragmented following the ICMP instructions sent by path MTU discovery. Luckily pmtu accounts for the 8 bytes header added for DSR, but it does not for any other possible header (like VLAN tags). This causes the packet to possibly be higher than the default network MTU and being dropped. I am not really sure which entity is dropping the packets, as I don't see them reaching Cilium. I've read somewhere that some routers drop packets with unknown options headers when they receive too many of them, so that might be a problem. I also tried to set Cilium's MTU to 1450, but the problem perists. Things seems to work when client and k8s cluster are on the same network, but if they are on two different VLANs (which can of course reach each other) then the packet is that bit larger that gets dropped, or at least this is my assumption ### How can we reproduce the issue? 1. Install Cilium with the following values on a multi-node k3s cluster ```yaml k8sServiceHost: k8s.kubelab.alea.lab k8sServicePort: 6443 kubeProxyReplacement: true ipv4NativeRoutingCIDR: "10.42.0.0/16" ipam: mode: kubernetes operator: clusterPoolIPv4PodCIDRList: "10.42.0.0/16" bpf: masquerade: false nodePort: enabled: true externalIPs: enabled: true l7Proxy: false hubble: relay: enabled: true ui: enabled: true l2announcements: enabled: true leaseDuration: 3s leaseRenewDeadline: 1.5s leaseRetryPeriod: 1s k8sClientRateLimit: qps: 170 burst: 200 healthChecking: true endpointHealthChecking: enabled: true tunnelProtocol: "" routingMode: native loadBalancer: mode: dsr dsrDispatch: opt socketLB: enabled: true hostNamespaceOnly: true autoDirectNodeRoutes: true MTU: 0 pmtuDiscovery: enabled: true ``` 2. Create a Cilium L2 announcement policy and LoadBalancer IP Pool 3. Deploy a UDP server with 3 replicas, and expose it with a LoadBalancer service 4. Send a UDP packet to the Loadbalancer IP with a size higher than 1500 ### Cilium Version cilium-cli: v0.18.3 compiled with go1.24.2 on linux/amd64 cilium image (default): v1.17.2 cilium image (stable): v1.17.3 cilium image (running): 1.17.3 ### Kernel Version Linux kubelab-w07 5.15.0-307.178.5.el8uek.x86_64 #2 SMP Wed Mar 19 13:00:52 PDT 2025 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux ### Kubernetes Version Client Version: v1.31.3 Kustomize Version: v5.4.2 Server Version: v1.32.3+k3s1 ### Regression _No response_ ### Sysdump _file is too large_ ### Relevant log output ```shell ``` ### Anything else? _No response_ ### Cilium Users Document - [ ] Are you a user of Cilium? signal.title: Gateway API: 503 connection timeout for same-node backends with L2 announcements and VXLAN tunnel mode
signal.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.20.0 and lower than v1.21.0 ### What happened? Gateway API with L2 announcements and VXLAN tunnel mode produces 503 "upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers. reset reason: connection timeout" for **all backend pods running on the same node that holds the L2 VIP lease**. Backend pods on other nodes work perfectly. The pattern is deterministic and follows the L2 lease holder: - When `node-a` holds the lease: all backends on `node-a` return 503, all backends on other nodes return 200 - When the lease moves (e.g. after a cilium restart): the failures follow the lease to the new holder node Envoy admin cluster stats confirm the pattern. Cross-node connectivity from regular pods (both with and without hostNetwork) works fine - this is specific to the envoy TPROXY path. `proxy-use-original-source-address` is hardcoded to `true` by the Helm chart when `kubeProxyReplacement: true`, and cannot be overridden via Helm values. This might be the root cause: envoy connects to same-node pods using the external client's source IP via TPROXY, and the response packet from the backend pod cannot route back to envoy correctly in VXLAN tunnel mode. **Please note that I did this research with Claude. I haven't tested the workaround yet.** ### How can we reproduce the issue? **Environment:** 3-node k3s cluster on Raspberry Pi (arm64), Ubuntu 26.04, kernel 7.0.0-1016-raspi **Cluster topology:** - `jarvis` (control-plane): 192.168.10.100, pod CIDR 10.0.1.0/24 - `node-a` (worker): 192.168.10.101, pod CIDR 10.0.2.0/24 - `node-b` (worker): 192.168.10.102, pod CIDR 10.0.0.0/24 **Steps:** 1. Install Cilium with the following Helm values: ```yaml kubeProxyReplacement: true gatewayAPI: enabled: true l2announcements: enabled: true l7Proxy: true bpf: tproxy: true devices: eth0 envoy: enabled: true securityContext: capabilities: envoy: - NET_ADMIN - SYS_ADMIN - NET_BIND_SERVICE keepCapNetBindService: true socketLB: enabled: true hostNamespaceOnly: false operator: replicas: 1 ``` 2. Create a CiliumLoadBalancerIPPool and CiliumL2AnnouncementPolicy: ```yaml apiVersion: cilium.io/v2alpha1 kind: CiliumLoadBalancerIPPool metadata: name: gateway-lan-pool spec: blocks: - start: 192.168.10.50 stop: 192.168.10.50 --- apiVersion: cilium.io/v2alpha1 kind: CiliumL2AnnouncementPolicy metadata: name: l2-announcement spec: interfaces: - ^eth0 loadBalancerIPs: true ``` 3. Create a Gateway with multiple HTTPS listeners and HTTPRoutes pointing to services on different nodes 4. Observe that backends on the node holding the L2 lease (check via `kubectl get leases -n kube-system | grep cilium-l2announce`) return 503, while backends on other nodes work **Verification commands:** ```bash # Check which node holds the lease kubectl get leases -n kube-system cilium-l2announce-default-cilium-gateway-http-gateway -o jsonpath='{.spec.holderIdentity}' # Check envoy cluster stats (run on the cilium pod of the lease-holding node) kubectl exec -n kube-system <cilium-pod> -- cilium-dbg envoy admin clusters | grep -E "(cx_connect_fail|rq_success|rq_error)" # Test cross-node connectivity from a regular pod (works fine) kubectl run tmp --rm -i --restart=Never --image=curlimages/curl -- curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://<backend-pod-ip>:<port> # Test from hostNetwork pod on the lease-holding node (also works fine) kubectl run tmp --rm -i --restart=Never --overrides='{"spec":{"hostNetwork":true,"nodeName":"<lease-holder>"}}' --image=curlimages/curl -- curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://<backend-pod-ip>:<port> ``` Both connectivity tests return 200, proving the issue is specific to the envoy TPROXY path, not general network connectivity. ### Relevant log output Curl response from the gateway for a same-node backend: ``` > GET / HTTP/1.1 > Host: argocd.jarvis-home.dev < HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable < content-length: 91 < content-type: text/plain < server: envoy upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers. reset reason: connection timeout ``` Envoy admin cluster stats for the failing backend (same node as lease holder): ``` argocd:argocd-server:80::10.0.2.4:8080::cx_active::0 argocd:argocd-server:80::10.0.2.4:8080::cx_connect_fail::14 argocd:argocd-server:80::10.0.2.4:8080::cx_total::14 argocd:argocd-server:80::10.0.2.4:8080::rq_active::0 argocd:argocd-server:80::10.0.2.4:8080::rq_error::14 argocd:argocd-server:80::10.0.2.4:8080::rq_success::0 argocd:argocd-server:80::10.0.2.4:8080::health_flags::healthy ``` Envoy admin cluster stats for a working backend (different node from lease holder): ``` technitium:technitium-svc:5380::10.0.1.131:5380::cx_active::6 technitium:technitium-svc:5380::10.0.1.131:5380::cx_connect_fail::0 technitium:technitium-svc:5380::10.0.1.131:5380::cx_total::14 technitium:technitium-svc:5380::10.0.1.131:5380::rq_active::0 technitium:technitium-svc:5380::10.0.1.131:5380::rq_error::0 technitium:technitium-svc:5380::10.0.1.131:5380::rq_success::67 technitium:technitium-svc:5380::10.0.1.131:5380::health_flags::healthy ``` Relevant cilium-config values: ``` routing-mode: tunnel tunnel-protocol: vxlan proxy-use-original-source-address: "true" enable-bpf-tproxy: "true" external-envoy-proxy: "true" kube-proxy-replacement: "true" gateway-api-hostnetwork-enabled: "false" bpf-lb-sock-hostns-only: "true" ``` ### Workaround Setting `proxy-use-original-source-address: "false"` in the cilium-config ConfigMap and restarting cilium + cilium-envoy DaemonSets resolves the issue. However, this cannot be done via Helm values because the chart hardcodes this to `true` when `kubeProxyReplacement: true`. ### Additional context - The issue was initially observed with technitium (DNS server) being the only pod on the control-plane node. When the L2 lease was on that node, only technitium failed. After a cilium restart moved the lease to a worker node, technitium started working but all worker-node backends broke. - `gatewayAPI.hostNetwork.enabled: true` has no effect when `external-envoy-proxy: true` (Cilium 1.20 default) - no dedicated gateway pods are created. - Related issues with similar symptoms but different root causes: #42325, #35559, #36004, #32592 ### Cilium Version 1.20.0 ### Kernel Version Linux drone-two 7.0.0-1016-raspi #16-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu Jul 23 22:56:44 UTC 2026 aarch64 GNU/Linux ### Kubernetes Version v1.36.3+k3s1 ### Regression _No response_ ### Sysdump [cilium-sysdump-20260818-144359.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31178210/cilium-sysdump-20260818-144359.zip) ### Relevant log output ```shell ``` ### Anything else? _No response_ ### Cilium Users Document - [ ] Are you a user of Cilium? Please add yourself to the [Users doc](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/USERS.md) ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

signal.title: Gateway API L7LB north-south traffic still dropped on 1.19.4 when LB VIP is announced on a VLAN subinterface (not a bridge)
signal.text: ### Is there an existing issue? - Related: #43819, #44187 (same north-south L7LB class). This adds a data point: the merged fixes #44658 / #45582 do **not** resolve it when the ingress device is a **VLAN subinterface** rather than a Linux bridge. ### What happened? External (north-south) TCP to a Gateway API L7 LoadBalancer VIP (an endpoint-less `type: LoadBalancer` Service flagged `[LoadBalancer, l7-load-balancer]`) is silently dropped before reaching Envoy, on **Cilium 1.19.4** — which contains both #44658 and #45582. The LB VIP is advertised via Cilium L2 announcements on a **VLAN subinterface** (`vsw0.4042@uplink0`, a Hetzner vSwitch VLAN), not a Linux bridge. `br_netfilter` is loaded and `net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables=1`. Observed on a request to the VIP from an external client and from a pod: - `cilium monitor -v` shows the redirect decision firing: `-> proxy port 19052 ... <client> -> <vip>:4318 tcp SYN` (this is new in 1.19.4; on 1.18.10 there was **no** datapath event at all — so #44658/#45582 did change behavior). - But the packet **never reaches the Envoy socket**: `tcpdump -i lo port 19052` shows zero traffic; no SYN-ACK egresses on any interface; the client times out. - `cilium monitor --type drop` shows nothing (drop is not in the BPF datapath). - Routing primitives are all correct: `ip rule` has `from all fwmark 0x200/0xf00 lookup 2004`, table `2004` has `local default dev lo`, Envoy is listening on `127.0.0.1:19052` (`SO_REUSEPORT`), `rp_filter=0`. - **Host-netns-originated** traffic to the same VIP works (socket-LB path). - Ruled out: host firewall (tested with it disabled), and `net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables=0` (tested — no change). This looks like the `MARK_MAGIC_TO_PROXY` + punt-to-stack / TPROXY-in-PREROUTING path from #36383, where the second PREROUTING pass is skipped (so the TPROXY rule never delivers to the socket). #44658 adds a hairpin fallback **gated on the device being a bridge**; our ingress device is a VLAN subinterface, so that fallback appears not to engage, and #45582’s `ctx->mark` fix doesn’t help here either. ### Question for maintainers Should the #44658 hairpin / #45582 fix also cover **non-bridge** netdevs (e.g. VLAN subinterfaces) when `br_netfilter` + `bridge-nf-call-iptables=1` cause `ip_sabotage_in()` to skip the second PREROUTING pass? Is there a recommended config to force the hairpin path for L7LB on such devices? ### Cilium Version 1.19.4 (upgraded from 1.18.10; behavior changed but issue persists) ### Kernel Version 6.8.0-117-generic (Ubuntu 24.04) ### Kubernetes Version v1.34 (k3s) ### Relevant config - `kubeProxyReplacement: true`, `l7Proxy: true`, `loadBalancer.l7.backend: envoy` - `l2announcements.enabled: true`; LB-IPAM VIP announced on a VLAN subinterface - Gateway API (native Cilium GatewayClass), TLS-terminating listeners on 443/4317/4318
